title: RAKF: Authorization Plane Analysis
description: Examine how RAKF evaluates access on TK5. Browse security tables, trace authorization decisions, identify misconfigurations.

steps.title: RAKF Overview
steps.screen:
RAKF — Resource Access Control Facility (TK5/MVS 3.8j)

RAKF is the security manager for TK5.
It controls:
- Who can log on (USERS table)
- What they can access (PROFILES table)
- What they can do (Operations flag, group access)

Unlike z/OS RACF, RAKF uses TEXT FILES:
  SYS1.SECURE.CNTL(USERS)
  SYS1.SECURE.CNTL(PROFILES)

All access decisions flow through these tables.
steps.expected: Understand RAKF as the authorization plane for TK5.
steps.hint: RAKF is simpler than RACF — editable text files instead of a database.

steps.title: Browse Users Table
steps.instruction: View all users and their privileges
steps.expected: See user entries with format: USERNAME GROUP PASSWORD OPERATIONS_FLAG
steps.hint: Y in the last column = Operations authority (like RACF SPECIAL). Passwords are cleartext!

steps.title: Identify Privileged Users
steps.screen:
In the USERS table, look for entries ending in Y:

HERC01   ADMIN   *CUL8TR  Y   ← Operations authority
IBMUSER  ADMIN   *SYS1    Y   ← Operations authority
HERC02   USER     PASS4U  N   ← Normal user

Operations=Y means:
- Bypass most access checks
- Equivalent to RACF SPECIAL attribute
- Highest privilege level
steps.expected: HERC01 and IBMUSER have Operations=Y — they are privileged users.
steps.hint: In an audit, flag every Operations=Y user and verify they need it.

steps.title: Browse Profiles Table
steps.expected: See profile entries with format: CLASS RESOURCE GROUP ACCESS
steps.hint: Blank group = universal access (UACC). Specific group entries override UACC.

steps.title: Trace Access Decision
steps.screen:
RAKF Access Evaluation Order:

1. Check user's Operations flag (Y = allow most access)
2. Check specific profile for CLASS+RESOURCE+GROUP
3. Check universal profile (blank group) for CLASS+RESOURCE
4. Default: NONE (deny)

Example for HERC02 accessing SYS1.PARMLIB:
  1. Operations=N — no bypass
  2. No DATASET SYS1.PARMLIB USER entry
  3. DATASET * (blank) = READ — ALLOWED

Gap: UACC=READ on DATASET * = any user can read system datasets.
steps.expected: Understand the RAKF access decision chain.
steps.hint: UACC=READ on 'DATASET *' is the biggest risk — every authenticated user can read everything.

steps.title: Check Dataset Protection
steps.expected: See dataset attributes. The RACF indicator should be set.
steps.hint: RAKF only protects datasets with the RACF indicator. Use CDSCB to set it.

steps.title: Security Assessment
steps.screen:
RAKF Security Assessment — TK5

[CRITICAL] Passwords stored in cleartext
[HIGH] UACC=READ on DATASET * (overly permissive)
[MEDIUM] Multiple Operations=Y users
[LOW] Default passwords in use

Remediation:
1. Restrict SYS1.SECURE.CNTL access
2. Set UACC=NONE on DATASET *, grant explicitly
3. Change default passwords
4. Set RACF indicator on all datasets
steps.hint: Same methodology applies to production RACF — different commands, same logic.
